ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=3$, and $BC=4$. Squares $ABMN$, $ACDE$, and $BCFG$ are constructed on the sides of $\triangle ABC$ on the same side as $AB$. Point $M$ is on side $FG$, $MN$ intersects $CF$ at point $P$, and $AN$ intersects $CD$ at point $Q$. $\triangle ABQ \cong \triangle NAP$; what is the area of quadrilateral $CPNQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABQ \cong \triangle NAP$,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ABQ} = S_{\triangle NAP}$,\\
hence $S_{\triangle ABC} = S_{\text{quadrilateral} CPNQ}$,\\
Since $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC = 3$, and $BC = 4$,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ABC} = \frac{1}{2}AC \cdot BC = 6$,\\
thus $S_{\text{quadrilateral} CPNQ} = \boxed{6}$.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 先描述图像：图中 AB 是水平底边，A 在左下、B 在右下，正方形 ABMN 在 AB 上方，N 在 A 的正上方、M 在 B 的正上方。点 C 位于正方形 ABMN 内部，AC 与 BC 在 C 处成直角。左侧有正方形 ACDE，右侧有正方形 BCFG；图中 CF 与 MN 相交于 P，CD 与 AN 相交于 Q。再推理：按指定坐标法，因 AC=3、BC=4 且 ∠ACB=90°，所以 AB=5。令 A=(0,0)，B=(5,0)，正方形 ABMN 在上方，则 N=(0,5)，M=(5,5)。点 C 满足 x^2+y^2=9，(x-5)^2+y^2=16，解得 C=(9/5,12/5)，取图中 AB 上方的点。由图中正方形方向，CF 垂直 BC，而 AC 也垂直 BC，所以 CF 平行 AC；又 CF 过 C，因此 CF 与 AC 在同一直线上。AC 的方程为 y=(4/3)x，与 MN 的 y=5 相交，得 P=(15/4,5)。同理，CD 垂直 AC，而 CB 也垂直 AC，所以 CD 平行 CB；又 CD 过 C，因此 CD 与 CB 在同一直线上。直线 CB 斜率为 -3/4，方程为 y-12/5=-(3/4)(x-9/5)，与 AN 的 x=0 相交，得 Q=(0,15/4)。现在用顶点 C(9/5,12/5)、P(15/4,5)、N(0,5)、Q(0,15/4) 的鞋带公式计算面积：正向和 = (9/5)(5)+(15/4)(5)+0+0=111/4；反向和 = (12/5)(15/4)+0+0+(15/4)(9/5)=63/4。面积 = 1/2 |111/4-63/4| = 1/2·12 = 6。因此四边形 CPNQ 的面积为 6。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=3$, and $BC=4$. Squares $ABMN$, $ACDE$, and $BCFG$ are constructed on the sides of $\triangle ABC$ on the same side as $AB$. Point $M$ is on side $FG$, $MN$ intersects $CF$ at point $P$, and $AN$ intersects $CD$ at point $Q$. $\triangle ABQ \cong \triangle NAP$; what is the area of quadrilateral $CPNQ$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABQ \cong \triangle NAP$,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ABQ} = S_{\triangle NAP}$,\\
hence $S_{\triangle ABC} = S_{\text{quadrilateral }CPNQ}$,\\
Since $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC = 3$, and $BC = 4$,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ABC} = \frac{1}{2}AC \cdot BC = 6$,\\
thus $S_{\text{quadrilateral }CPNQ} = \boxed{6}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and C is in the middle slightly above; AC and BC form a right angle at C. The visible point P is at the intersection of the upper side MN and line CF, and A, C, P are on the same straight line; point Q is at the intersection of the left side AN and line CD, and B, C, Q are on the same straight line. The figure also marks the squares ABMN, ACDE, BCFG constructed with AB, AC, BC as sides.
Reasoning: Because ACDE and BCFG are squares, CD is parallel to CB, and CF is parallel to CA, which is consistent with B, C, Q being collinear and A, C, P being collinear in the figure. It is known that triangle ABQ congruent to triangle NAP, therefore their areas are equal. By the division of the figure, triangle ABQ can be divided into triangle ABC and triangle ACQ; triangle NAP can be divided into triangle ACQ and quadrilateral CPNQ. Thus [ABC] + [ACQ] = [ACQ] + [CPNQ]; canceling the common [ACQ], we get [CPNQ] = [ABC]. Also because angle ACB = 90 degrees, AC = 3, BC = 4, so [ABC] = 1/2 * 3 * 4 = 6. Therefore the area of quadrilateral CPNQ is 6.
